transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess what finally made me come in is that I’ve been having trouble keeping my place with ordinary work things. I’m a receptionist, so I’m scheduling appointments all day, checking details, making sure I didn’t put someone in the wrong slot or miss a message, and lately I’ll be in the middle of doing something and suddenly realize my mind has slipped off somewhere else.

Like, I’ll be entering an appointment or working on the lobby displays, and instead of just doing the task, I’m thinking about what I might have overlooked. Did I forget to tell someone something, did I miss a detail, did I do that last step correctly — that kind of thing. And then I lose my place and have to go back and check where I was. It’s not dramatic, exactly, but it’s frustrating and it’s started to feel like it’s getting in the way enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your mind slipping off during tasks?

It’s been about nine months now, I think. I can kind of trace it back pretty clearly to that overnight detention and the paperwork mix-up around it. After that happened, it was like my brain just stopped trusting that things were handled, if that makes sense. Since then, during normal tasks, I’ll catch myself drifting into checking or replaying whether something got missed. So, yes—around nine months.
When your mind slips off during tasks, do you ever find yourself having thoughts or mental images that feel intrusive, upsetting, or hard to control?

Yes, I think so. I don’t know if I’d call them images exactly, but the thoughts feel intrusive in the sense that they don’t really wait for me to invite them in. I’ll be doing something simple, and then it’s like, did I handle that message right, did I tell the right person, did I double-check that name, and then I try to talk myself down.

I’ll literally think, Sunny, it’s handled, you already did that, move on. But it doesn’t always move on. The thought keeps looping, and then it sort of branches off into another worry, and then another one. Before I know it, I’m checking details in my head over and over instead of just finishing what I was doing. It’s upsetting mostly because I know I’m trying to be reasonable, but it feels hard to shut off once it starts.

When you have these intrusive thoughts, do you find yourself doing anything specific—like checking, counting, or repeating things in your mind—to try to make the thoughts go away or feel more certain?

Yes… not counting, no, and not repeating words exactly. It’s more like mental checking. I’ll try to reassure myself — like, Sunny, it’s handled, you already did that, you don’t need to go back over it — but then the thought doesn’t really settle.

It’ll start with one thing, like whether I entered something correctly or passed along a message, and then almost immediately it turns into another concern. Like, okay, but what if I wrote the time down wrong, or what if I forgot to note something important, or what if the person at the desk misunderstood me. And then I’m going through the details in my head over and over, trying to feel certain enough to let it go.

So it’s not a ritual exactly, at least I don’t think of it that way, but I do get stuck checking in my mind. And the frustrating part is that telling myself it’s fine doesn’t really make it stop. It just loops for a while.

Do you ever find yourself going back to physically check things—like messages, appointment details, or paperwork—because your thoughts won’t let you feel sure, even if you logically know you already handled them?

Yes, I do sometimes go back and check physically, especially with scheduling things. Like, I can know I put an appointment in, or that I wrote down the right time, but then I’ll still open it back up or look at the paper again because I can’t quite get that settled feeling.

I’m still showing up and I’m getting through the day, so it’s not like everything has fallen apart, but things take longer than they used to. Scheduling is probably the biggest one, because I double-check myself so much now. I’ll check the name, then the time, then whether I put it in the right place, and then sometimes I’ll circle back again because I start doubting whether I really checked it carefully enough the first time.

And it’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know how to do my job. I’ve done this kind of work for a long time. But lately even simple things feel slower because I’m trying to make sure I didn’t miss something.

I’ve also had it happen with the lobby displays — like arranging flyers or notices. I’ll lose track of what I was doing because my mind gets caught up in whether I handled some detail correctly, and then I realize the display looks off or I put something in the wrong spot, and I have to redo parts of it. So, yes, I do check, and it does interfere, just not to the point where I can’t function at all.

Do you feel driven to perform any specific mental acts or behaviors over and over again, even if you don’t want to, because you feel like you have to in order to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce your anxiety?

I wouldn’t say it feels like, if I don’t do this exact thing then something terrible will definitely happen, not in a very specific way. It’s more that I feel this pressure to get certainty, if that makes sense.

Like I can tell myself, Sunny, it’s handled, you already did it, there’s no reason to keep going over it. But the thought doesn’t really listen. It keeps looping, and then pretty soon I’ve gone from one concern to another — first it’s one detail, then it’s another detail, then I’m reviewing the whole thing in my head again.

So I do end up checking details mentally over and over, even when I don’t want to. It’s not because I want to be doing it, and it’s not helpful after a point. I’m just trying to calm the anxiety enough to feel like I can move on, but sometimes the checking becomes the thing I can’t stop doing.
Do these thoughts and the need to check things over and over cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your life outside of work, like with family, friends, or things you used to enjoy?

It does distress me, yes… mostly because I can feel myself taking longer with things I used to just do without thinking so much. I’m still showing up, I’m still getting through the day, and I don’t think anyone would look at me and say I’m falling apart or anything like that. But scheduling, especially, has become slower because I double-check myself so much.

Like I’ll put something in, then I’ll go back and check the time, then the name, then whether I entered it in the right spot, and then sometimes I’m still not settled, so I’ll look again. And I know that sounds small, but when it happens over and over during the day, it wears on me. It makes me feel less confident, like I can’t just trust myself the way I used to.

And with other tasks, too, like the lobby displays — flyers, notices, arranging things so they look neat — I’ve lost track of what I was doing because I got caught up worrying about whether I handled some other detail right. Then I’ll step back and realize something looks off, or I put something in the wrong place, and I have to redo parts of it.

Outside of work… I don’t know that it’s taken over everything, but it does leave me drained and frustrated. It’s more that my workday feels harder than it should, and then I carry that feeling with me afterward.
Do you feel like you have to keep checking things or going over them in your mind to make sure nothing bad happens or to reduce the anxiety that builds up when you don’t?

Yes… more to reduce the anxiety, I think. I don’t always have a clear picture of some bad thing happening, like, “If I don’t check this, this exact disaster will happen.” It’s not usually that specific. It’s more that the uncertainty starts building and I can’t get it to quiet down.

I can tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled. You already did it. You checked it.” And part of me knows that. But the thought keeps looping anyway, like it doesn’t accept that answer. Then I’ll start with one concern, like whether I got the time right, and before I know it I’m thinking about the name, and then whether I put it in the right place, and then whether I was distracted when I checked it the first time. It just kind of branches out.

So yes, I do end up going over details in my mind over and over, not because I want to, but because I’m trying to get that anxious feeling to settle enough that I can move on. Sometimes it helps for a moment, but then the doubt comes back again.
Do you feel like you have to do your checking or mental reassurance in a certain way or for a certain amount of time, like it has to feel 'just right' or else you have to start over?

Not really in a strict way, no. It’s not like I have to check it exactly three times, or do it in a certain order, or start all over because I didn’t think it the “right” way. It’s more… I keep trying to get my mind to accept that it’s okay.

I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled. You already looked at it.” And I’ll mean it. But then the thought just keeps circling back, like it didn’t land. So I’ll go over the detail again in my head, and then another detail pops up, and then another one, until suddenly I’m mentally checking the whole thing over and over.

So it’s not a ritual exactly, at least I don’t think of it that way. It’s more that I’m chasing that feeling of certainty, or relief, and sometimes I don’t get it. Or I get it for a second and then the worry starts up again.
